newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- new issues dominate.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- new issues dominate.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds were unchanged in quiet secondary action Wednesday, as the day's large slate of new issues dominated action, traders said.
In the largest issue of the day, JP Morgan Securities Inc. tentatively priced a $528 million New York City Municipal Assistance Corporation offering Wednesday at a top yield of 5.175 percent in 2005.
The firm said it already found buyers for $121 million during a one-day retail order period Tuesday.
Many traders, however, said they were watching other new issues more closely because the MAC deal is structured with only short maturities.
Morgan Stanley & Co. tentatively priced $129 million Michigan Hospital Authority bonds at a top yield of 6.05 percent in 2028.
Also Wednesday, Goldman Sachs & Co is expected to price $500 million Chicago School Reform Board of Trustees unlimited tax general obligation bonds.
The largest competitive deal is a $44 million Norfolk, Va., issue at 1030 EDT.
In other new supply news, Lehman Brothers said Wednesday it had still not decided whether to price a $932 million Port Authority of New York and New Jersey airport deal this week or next.

In the government cash market, the benchmark 30-year bond was down 5/32 at 94-21/32 to yield 7.06 percent. Market analysts attributed some of the erosion to nervousness ahead of Wednesday's $12.5 billion five-year note auction.
In debt futures, the municipal contract lost 1/32 at 112-30/32, while June T-bond contract closed down 3/32 at 108-1/32. The MOB spread widened to 157 ticks from 155 at the close on Tuesday.
In the muni secondary, bids were unchanged at 5.93 percent for Denver Airport MBIA 5-1/2s of 2025. Texas Turnpike Authority FGIC 5.0s of 2025 were also flat, at 5.84 percent.
